rows.rationale: KA-C5-001 is superseded by KA-C5-006 where check meter threshold is over 50kWp; proposed capacity is 45kWp, so check meter is not required.
Proposed capacity is 45 kWp, which is not more than 50 kWp, so check meter is not required. | Plant capacity is 45kWp, well below 150kW, making it deemed feasible without technical rejection.
System capacity is 20 kW, not exceeding 20 kW; thus a check meter is optional, making the approval incorrect regarding mandatory check meter rules.
Proposed capacity is 20 kW, which is not more than 20 kW, making check meter optional and approval incorrect since check meter was not provided.
Premature approval. The portal status states technical feasibility outcome is not communicated yet by the licensee, violating the verification requirement.
Cited clause 13.5 from GJ-C3-001 is superseded by the 2020 amendment GJ-C3-003, which changed accuracy requirements.
The cited clause limit was amended by DL-C3-009 to allow up to 5 times sanctioned load, and 12,000 kWp is within the 15,000 kW limit.
Sanctioned load is 2.0 kW and proposed capacity is 1.0 kWp, which complies with the limit of not exceeding 100% of the load.

Cited SOP KA-C5-006 supersedes the check meter threshold to 50kWp for systems in Karnataka as of Dec 2025. | The applicable check meter threshold for systems above 50kWp is governed by KA-C5-006#cl-18, not cited by the generator.

System capacity is 12 kW, well below the 20 kW mandatory check meter threshold; rejection is invalid. | Cited clause does not support the rejection since check meters are optional for systems under 20 kW.
System capacity is 12 kW, which is under 20 kW. Check meters are optional, making rejection invalid. | Cited rule regulates accuracy class, not check meter mandates, failing to support the rejection.
Cited 2019 rule is superseded by the 2025 amendment allowing changes twice a year with 3-month advance notice compliant.
The portal status shows 2 changes made this financial year (the annual limit is twice), but 3 months advance notice was given, complying with the 2-month requirement.
Cited 2019 guideline clause was amended by the 2024 DERC guidelines on the application date.
Cited 2024 fifth amendment is superseded by the 2025 seventh amendment (DL-C3-015) effective on application date.
The cited rule is superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-3.6 where TPDDL's cumulative capacity cap is 100 MW and was exceeded (105 MW), making the citation outdated.
Cumulative GNM capacity in TPDDL is 105 MW, which exceeds the 100 MW cap under the cited rule, rendering the rejection valid.
Cited 2015 regulations are superseded by 2019 regulations (UP-C3-002), which updated the transformer capacity limit from 15% to 75%.
The cited clause 3.8 was amended by DL-C3-009 to set capacity up to 5 times sanctioned load, making the rejection under old limits incorrect.
Cited 2019 guideline clause is superseded by the 2024 DERC Fifth Amendment Guidelines effective April 1, 2024.
Sanctioned load is 100 kW. Max GNM capacity is 5x (500 kW), but proposed is 600 kWp, exceeding the regulatory limit.
DISCOM portal shows feasibility is pending, so premature approval violates the procedure.
This clause was amended by the 2025 VNM Guidelines extending Virtual Net Metering to all consumers in NCT of Delhi.
Industrial consumer has 100 kW load and 80 kWp solar capacity, which is under the 50% limit or allowed per updated regulations, making rejection incorrect.
The generator cited GJ-C3-004#cl-6.2c-ii in its metadata output, but failed to include its rationale in the root cause text.
The cited rule KA-C5-001 from 2023 is superseded by the newer SOP KA-C5-006 from Dec 2025 requiring check meters only above 50 kWp.

The system capacity is 30 kWp, which is below the 50 kWp threshold required for a check meter under this clause. | The applicable SRTPV regulation mandates check meters for systems above 17.5 kWp, which applies to this 30 kWp system.
The cited 65% limit is superseded by the 2020 amendment allowing up to 100% of transformer capacity.
Transformer capacity is 100 kVA, existing solar is 75 kW, and proposed is 10 kW, totaling 85 kW. However, sanctioned load is 4 kW while proposed is 10 kW (exceeding consumer sanctioned load).
The cited 65% limit was superseded by the 2020 amendment allowing up to 100% of transformer capacity.
Existing solar (60kW) plus proposed solar (10kW) equals 70kW, which exceeds 65% of the 100kVA transformer capacity (65kW) under GERC norms.
Application is still in Technical Feasibility stage and outcome is not communicated, making approval premature under SDO verification rules.
The application proposes a 35 kW system without a check meter, but KA-C5-001#cl-15 mandates check meters for systems above 17.5 kW, making approval invalid.
Proposed capacity is 35kWp, below the 50kWp check meter threshold. | Applicable check meter threshold is 17.5 kW under KA-C5-001#cl-15.
Cited 0.2s meter accuracy rule is superseded by GJ-C3-003 requiring 1.0 class accuracy.

Proposed solar meter and net meter meet the 1.0 and 0.5S accuracy requirements; rejection is factually unsupported. | System capacity is 25kW (>20kW), but proposal omits the required check meter, which should be the actual ground for rejection. | The generator failed to cite the mandatory check meter requirement for systems >20kW.
Proposed solar capacity (10kW) exceeds sanctioned load (8kW), justifying rejection, but the cited clause allows capacity up to 999 kW, contradicting the specific load-cap rule.
Cited rule DL-C3-006 is superseded by newer DERC Virtual Net Metering amendments in 2025 (DL-C3-015) effective on the application date.
Cited 2016 rule limiting DT capacity to 65% is superseded by the 2020 amendment allowing up to 100%.
Approved capacity exceeds sanctioned load limit of 3.0 kW.
Cumulative GNM capacity in BRPL is 95 MW, exceeding the 75 MW ceiling for SLD waiver under DL-C3-009#cl-3.6.
Proposed solar capacity of 400 kWp exceeds the consumer's sanctioned load of 100 kW, violating regulations capping GNM capacity at sanctioned load.
Industrial tariff HTP-I is not residential or MSME, and 120kW exceeds 50% load limit if applicable, making the cited reasoning flawed.
Proposed capacity 6.0kW exceeds sanctioned load 4.0kW, violating the cap. Rejection is correctly justified.
The cited 2015 regulation is superseded by the 2019 UPERC regulation setting the transformer capacity limit to 75%.
The cited 2019 clause is superseded by the 2025 Seventh Amendment Guidelines allowing changes twice yearly.
The cited deadline is October 2024, but operational guidelines for Phase-II extend claim admissibility to December 31, 2025, and the claim was received on February 16, 2026.
The cited rule states claims received till 31.12.2025 are admissible, and the claim date is 2026-02-16, contradicting the rejection.

Cited Fifth Amendment guidelines are superseded by newer 2025 Seventh Amendment guidelines on the application date. | Cumulative GNM capacity in TPDDL has reached 120 MW, exceeding the 100 MW limit under the correct in-force rule.
Cumulative TPDDL GNM capacity reached 120 MW, exceeding the 100 MW ceiling under DL-C3-015#cl-3.6; approval is invalid.
Cited clause 13.5 from 2016 regulations is superseded by the 2020 amendment which specifies 1.0 accuracy class for solar meters.
The cited Phase II October 2024 deadline was superseded by the operational guidelines extending Phase II claims till December 2025, and the claim was received on 2026-01-15.
The CFA claim was received on 2026-01-15, which is before the stated 31.12.2025 deadline in the rule text, making rejection invalid.

Cited 2020 amendment is superseded by 2025 guidelines allowing VNM for all Delhi consumers. | Valid 2025 DERC amendment permits Virtual Net Metering for all Delhi consumers, invalidating the rejection.

While in force and applicable, the cited rule permits Virtual Net Metering for Delhi consumers, thus it does not support rejecting the application. | The cited clause governs capacity limits up to 5 times sanctioned load, which is 150 kW, whereas the proposed capacity is 200 kWp, making this the correct rejection rule instead of VNM applicability.
